jobs.skipReason: The honest answer to "why did you ok this": it never was. Killed the same day it surfaced (Nov 4) on one line in the posting: "Active Secret Clearance or higher." You'd have to walk in already holding a federal Secret clearance — and clearances aren't something an applicant can go out and get; the government issues them through an employer, after hiring you into a cleared job. A posting demanding one you don't have is a wall with no door.
skipExtra: Second wall: it requires a Bachelor's degree — yours is the Associate.
Third: full-time on-site in Washington DC at $70,000 — a daily train commute on a thin salary.
Fourth: the posting itself warns the job may never be filled if their contract isn't awarded.

Why it looked ok'd: the kill note that day listed everything attractive first — junior title, decent band, your cert satisfying their cert line — and buried the one fatal line at the bottom. Read quickly, that reads like an endorsement. That was a presentation failure, and it's exactly what this console format fixes: verdict first, the reason first, details after. This posting will not be shown to you again.
jobs.tombstone: Killed Nov 4, 2026 — "Active Secret Clearance" wall; the presentation lesson lives in the card.
